newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat jointing stays ahead of average.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat jointing stays ahead of average.

text.p: Warm weather during the week ended Sunday allowed jointing to continue to advance ahead of average, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.
But the report said insect pressure was on the rise with producers reporting infestations of greenbugs, aphids and armyworms. Diseases also began to show up in selected fields.
Oklahoma wheat condition was rated 13 percent excellent, 70 good, 15 fair and two percent poor. That compared to last week's rating of 15 percent excellent, 68 good, 14 fair and three poor.
Wheat acreage jointing was reported at 37 percent, versus 13 last year and 27 percent for the five-year average.

Pasture condition increased slightly with the warmer temperatures and was rated three percent excellent, 48 good, 39 fair and 10 poor. That compared to the previous week's rating three percent excellent, 49 good, 38 fair, nine poor and one very poor.
Livestock condition was rated six percent excellent, 69 good, 21 fair and four poor.
